- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing mean reversion in the middle-to-late horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+ → 76+ forecast) are common, followed by underestimation in subsequent days.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history includes high prices (e.g., 74–75 range).
- Forecasts often fail to adjust downward when true outcomes show early mean reversion (e.g., 75 → 72–73).
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually converge but lag behind true values by 2–5 days.
- Model underreacts to downward momentum in recent history, especially when true prices drop below 70–71.
- Forecasts show strong persistence of recent highs, even when true prices are trending lower.
